source_text: Καὶ ὅτι δύο παρουσίας συμβολικῶς γενήσεσθαι τούτου τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ὑπὸ Μωσέως προελέγετο, προεῖπον διὰ τοῦ συμβόλου τῶν ἐν τῇ νηστείᾳ προσφερομένων τράγων. Καὶ πάλιν ἐν οἷς ἐποίησαν Μωσῆς καὶ Ἰησοῦς τὸ αὐτὸ προκηρυσσόμενον συμβολικῶς ἦν καὶ λεγόμενον. Ὁ μὲν γὰρ αὐτῶν τὰς χεῖρας ἐκτείνας ἐπὶ τοῦ βουνοῦ μέχρις ἑσπέρας ἔμενεν, ὑποβασταζομένων τῶν χειρῶν, ὃ οὐδενὸς ἄλλου τύπον δείκνυσιν ἢ τοῦ σταυροῦ, ὁ δὲ τῷ Ἰησοῦ ὀνόματι μετονομασθεὶς ἦρχε τῆς μάχης, καὶ ἐνίκα Ἰσραήλ. Ἦν δὲ καὶ τοῦτο ἐπ᾿ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν ἁγίων ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων καὶ προφητῶν τοῦ θεοῦ νοῆσαι γεγενημένον, ὅτι ἀμφότερα τὰ μυστήρια εἷς αὐτῶν βαστάσαι οὐκ ἦν δυνατός, λέγω δὲ τὸν τύπον τοῦ σταυροῦ καὶ τὸν τύπον τῆς τοῦ ὀνόματος ἐπικλήσεως· ἑνὸς γὰρ μόνου ἡ ἰσχὺς αὕτη ἐστὶ καὶ ἦν καὶ ἔσται, οὗ καὶ τὸ ὄνομα πᾶσα ἀρχὴ δέδιεν, ὠδίνουσα ὅτι δι᾿ αὐτοῦ καταλύεσθαι μέλλουσιν. Ὁ οὖν παθητὸς ἡμῶν καὶ σταυρωθεὶς Χριστὸς οὐ κατηράθη ὑπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἀλλὰ μόνος σώσειν τοὺς μὴ ἀφισταμένους τῆς πίστεως αὐτοῦ ἐδήλου. Καὶ τοὺς ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ δὲ σωθέντας, ὅτε ἀπώλλυντο τὰ πρωτότοκα τῶν Αἰγυπτίων, τὸ τοῦ πάσχα ἐρρύσατο αἷμα, τὸ ἑκατέρωσε τῶν σταθμῶν καὶ τοῦ ὑπερθύρου χρισθέν . Ἦν γὰρ τὸ πάσχα ὁ Χριστός, ὁ τυθεὶς ὕστερον , ὡς καὶ Ἡσαςΐας ἔφη· Αὐτὸς ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη [Is., LIII, 7]. Καὶ ὅτι ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ πάσχα συνελάβετε αὐτὸν καὶ ὁμοίως ἐν τῷ πάσχα ἐσταυρώσατε, γέγραπται. Ὡς δὲ τοὺς ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ ἔσωσε τὸ αἷμα τοῦ πάσχα, οὕτως καὶ τοῦς πιστεύσαντας ῥύσεται ἐκ θανάτου τὸ αἷμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Ἔμελλεν οὖν ὁ θεὸς πλανᾶσθαι, εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον τοῦτο ἐπὶ τῶν θυρῶν ἐγεγόνει ; Οὔ φημι ἐγώ, ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι προεκήρυσσε τὴν μέλλουσαν δι᾿ αἵματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ γενήσεσθαι σωτηρίαν τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων. Καὶ γὰρ τὸ σύμβολον τοῦ κοκκίνου σπαρτίου, οὗ ἔδωκαν ἐν Ἱεριχῶ οἱ ἀπὸ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναυῆ πεμφθέντες κατάσκοποι Ῥαὰβ τῇ πόρνῃ, εἰπόντες προσδῆσαι αὐτὸ τῇ θυρίδι, δι᾿ ἧς αὐτοὺς ἐχάλασεν ὅπως λάθωσι τοὺς πολεμίους , ὁμοίως τὸ σύμβολον τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐδήλου, δι᾿ οὗ οἱ πάλαι πόρνοι καὶ ἄδικοι ἐκ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν σώζονται, ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν λαβόντες καὶ μηκέτι ἁμαρτάνοντες.
pass_a_gloss: And that the two comings of this Christ were symbolically going to happen, and were spoken beforehand by Moses, I said through the symbol of the goats brought near in the fast. And again in what Moses and Jesus did, the same thing was proclaimed symbolically and spoken. For one of them, having stretched out his hands on the mountain until evening, remained, his hands being supported, which shows the type of no other thing than the cross; and the one who was renamed Jesus led the battle and conquered Israel. And it was also this that had been noticed by both of those holy men and prophets of God, that both mysteries - I mean the type of the cross and the type of the invocation of the name - one of them was not able to bear; for the power of one alone is and was and will be, whose name every ruler fears, being in pain because they are going to be destroyed through him. Therefore, our Christ who suffered and was crucified was not cursed by the law, but showed that he alone will save those who do not turn away from his faith. And also those who were saved in Egypt, when the firstborn of the Egyptians were being destroyed, the blood of the passover protected, the blood having been smeared on the doorposts and the lintel. For the passover was Christ, who was slain later, as Isaiah also said: He was led like a sheep to slaughter. And that on the day of the passover you seized him and similarly crucified him on the passover, it is written. And just as the blood of the passover saved those in Egypt, so also the blood of Christ will save from death those who believe. Therefore, was God going to be deceived if this sign had not been on the doors? I say not, but that he proclaimed beforehand the salvation that was going to happen through the blood of Christ to the race of men. And also the symbol of the scarlet cord, which those sent by Jesus the son of Nun as spies gave to Rahab the prostitute in Jericho, saying to fasten it to the window through which they let her down so that they might escape the enemies, similarly showed the symbol of the blood of Christ, through which the former prostitutes and unrighteous from all nations are saved, having received forgiveness of sins and no longer sinning.

bible_refs.note: He was led like a sheep to slaughter

pass_b_english: I have already shown that the two comings of this Christ were foretold symbolically by Moses through the figure of the two goats offered in the fast.

Again, the same mystery was proclaimed symbolically in what Moses and Jesus did: Moses stretched out his hands on the hill until evening, his hands being held up, which displays the type of nothing other than the cross; and Jesus, who had been renamed Jesus, led the battle and conquered Israel.

Both of those holy men and prophets of God perceived this as well: neither one of them could bear both mysteries — I mean the type of the cross and the type of the invocation of the name — for the power belongs to one alone, and was, and is, and will be, whose name every ruler fears, writhing in anguish because they are destined to be destroyed through him.
Therefore our Christ, who suffered and was crucified, was not cursed by the law, but he alone demonstrated that he will save those who do not turn away from his faith.

Likewise those who were saved in Egypt when the firstborn of the Egyptians perished were protected by the blood of the Passover, smeared on the doorposts and the lintel; for the Passover was Christ, who was slain later, as Isaiah also said: "He was led like a sheep to slaughter" (Isaiah 53:7).
And that you seized him on the day of the Passover and likewise crucified him on the Passover is written.
Just as the blood of the Passover saved those in Egypt, so also the blood of Christ will rescue from death those who believe.

Would God have been deceived if this sign had not been placed on the doors? I do not say so; rather, he proclaimed beforehand the salvation that was going to come to the human race through the blood of Christ.

And the symbol of the scarlet cord, which the spies sent by Jesus son of Nun gave to Rahab the prostitute in Jericho, telling her to fasten it to the window through which she let them down so that they might escape their enemies, similarly signified the blood of Christ, through which former prostitutes and the unrighteous from all nations are saved, having received forgiveness of sins and no longer sinning.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a polished, accurate translation that preserves all theological distinctions and agency. Scripture citation (Isaiah 53:7) is correctly identified and applied to the quoted text. The title 'Symbolic Representations of Christ' accurately reflects the content of the chapter.
